approach: At the exact instant a 45° projectile lands, its velocity has turned enough to become perpendicular to the initial velocity, making the dot product zero.

steps.text: Write the initial velocity and the velocity at time t in components, using the 45° launch angle.
Compute the dot product of the initial velocity with the velocity at time t.
Set this dot product to zero and solve for t.
Compare this time with the time of flight of a projectile launched at 45°.
steps.equation: T = 2u·sin45°/g = u√2/g, equal to the t found above

steps.text: Since the dot product becomes zero exactly at t = T, which is a real, nonzero time reached during the flight, u·v can indeed be zero, so the Assertion is true, and the Reason states the general condition for a zero dot product, which is exactly why this happens.
steps.why_this_step: The perpendicularity condition in the Reason is the same condition solved for t in the earlier steps.

final_answer.value: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the dot product can never be zero during flight because velocity never fully reverses direction, missing that perpendicularity alone is enough.
Judging the Assertion false since u and v seem to point in roughly the same general direction through most of the flight.
